snapshotContract.rawValues: string or null; null means the key is absent
snapshotContract.serialization: A JSON envelope escapes NUL and lone surrogates before any future native text storage; the raw values are never normalized.
snapshotContract.sourceReads: Two synchronous passes detect differences between reads. They are not an atomic snapshot across tabs or processes.
snapshotContract.databaseWrites: Only the explicitly called SQLite snapshot repository writes the preserved envelope. Production startup does not activate it; native CI uses generated synthetic values.
snapshotContract.errorPolicy: Denied or unexpected reads and any observed source change abort capture without substituting empty data. Errors do not include raw values.

activationGates: Pass Android and iOS protocol 5 tests for atomic mutable batches, revision conflicts, committed process restart, interrupted updates and exact recovery before enabling writers.
Declare production database ownership and path selection and coordinate every source context; repository guards are not cross-tab or cross-process locks.
Integrate bootstrap before App and ExperienceLayer parse, normalize or write personal state; pause every legacy writer during capture, preparation, final source comparison and commit.
Retain the immutable first raw copy and use the valid SQLite completion marker and latest committed revision as authority. Never silently fall back to stale legacy storage after cutover.

Integrate asynchronous durable writes into the UI, maps, preferences and validated backup imports; acknowledge persistence only after successful SQLite commit, and define retry and conflict recovery without dropping pending user changes.
Preserve raw values and explicitly report rejected, filtered, normalized or unmapped records instead of replacing them with sanitized defaults.
Maintain legacy and v1-v4 backup imports and define preference preservation and typed-title identity in a future versioned export contract.
Validate disk failures, concurrent external source writers, startup recovery UX and app interruption through the complete bootstrap and UI integration on real devices before activating migration.
scope: Local-first native preparation; no account or backend required.

coordinatorContract.backend: localStorage; no SQLite cutover in this change
coordinatorContract.allowedKeys: the same six keys as the raw snapshot registry
coordinatorContract.pauseScope: this JavaScript instance only; other tabs, processes or direct external storage writes are not locked
coordinatorContract.batchGuard: validates all keys and holds the write guard across original-value reads, every write, and rollback
coordinatorContract.capture: only the current pause owner can capture or compare raw values; observed external changes abort comparison
coordinatorContract.pauseOwnership: stale handles cannot resume or close another pause; failed captures retain the pause
coordinatorContract.closedLegacyAccess: once closed, the facade refuses reads as well as writes and has no reopen method
coordinatorContract.cutoverAuthority: a future bootstrap must first verify the durable database completion marker and new repository before closing legacy access; the in-memory phase is not that marker
coordinatorContract.startup: creating the shared coordinator performs no storage access; production startup does not request a pause or capture yet

nativeValidation.scope: The integrated legacy facade and synthetic native SQLite probe passed. Personal storage migration remains disabled.

sqliteSnapshotContract.activation: Explicit API on an already-open, exclusively owned connection; no global storage access or DB selection at import/construction.
sqliteSnapshotContract.rawPreservation: Canonical JSON envelope preserving all six raw strings or missing keys; stored values are never parsed, sanitized or normalized.
sqliteSnapshotContract.boundedNativeCalls: Each text chunk is at most 16384 UTF-16 units. Valid surrogate pairs are never split; JSON escapes NUL and lone surrogates. Each native call contains one statement and each chunk read has one bound ordinal.
sqliteSnapshotContract.oversizePolicy: Reject before any database access; never truncate or discard values.
sqliteSnapshotContract.integrity: SHA-256 over UTF-8 of the complete canonical serialized envelope, exact UTF-16 length, bounded metadata, contiguous chunks and strict schema validation.
sqliteSnapshotContract.transaction: Create both tables, metadata and all bound chunks in one explicit transaction; verify before commit and again in a second transaction after commit.
sqliteSnapshotContract.retries: An identical copy is idempotent without rewriting; a different snapshot cannot replace the first preserved copy.
sqliteSnapshotContract.failurePolicy: No empty-default fallback. Roll back only a transaction begun by this operation, preserve primary failure, hide native errors that may echo private values, and refuse reuse after uncertain database operations until the owner closes/reopens.
sqliteSnapshotContract.ownershipLimit: The in-memory operation guard protects one repository instance; callers must own the entire native connection and coordinate other contexts. This repository is not the future migrated-data repository or migration completion marker.
sqliteSnapshotContract.databaseSchemaVersion: Does not change PRAGMA user_version or touch unrelated tables.

preparedNativeAudit.source: generated synthetic values and a paused in-memory source only
preparedNativeAudit.payload: Greater than 2 Mi UTF-16 units, all six exact raw values, invalid JSON, absence, empty and JSON-null text, future IDs, Unicode, NUL, CRLF, lone surrogates and preferences.
preparedNativeAudit.migrationInterruption: Keep the actual migration schema, values and completion marker uncommitted in launch 2. Interrupt only the verified fresh audit app; launch 3 requires rollback and commits a guarded retry.
preparedNativeAudit.mutableWriteRestart: Launch 3 updates several keys with the actual writeBatch API, requires revision 1, verifies an identical no-op and rejects a stale expected revision. Reopen the native connection, then launch 4 verifies the same committed values in a fresh process.
preparedNativeAudit.mutableWriteInterruption: Launch 4 uses actual prepareWrite, verifies changed chunks and receipt revision 2 while the transaction remains open. After interruption, launch 5 must recover all revision-1 values, then retry and durably reopen revision 2 with the immutable original unchanged.
preparedNativeAudit.activation: CI generated bundle only; production entry, six storage keys, package identity and installed app version are unchanged.

lastValidatedNative.scope: Synthetic six-key data only; migration preparation and its native recovery passed. Production personal SQLite startup remains disabled.

transactionalMigrationContract.activation: Explicit preparation API on an open, exclusively owned native connection. No DB selection, browser storage access or migration occurs during import, construction or production startup.
transactionalMigrationContract.versionAuthority: Namespaced schema_version in cv_personal_migration, committed with state=complete and six entries. The repository leaves global PRAGMA user_version and unrelated tables unchanged.
transactionalMigrationContract.dataModel: Six ordered key slots retaining raw string or absence. JSON encodes the raw string/null itself; it does not parse the JSON stored inside those strings. Unknown IDs, malformed JSON, preference fields and all UTF-16 values remain exact.
transactionalMigrationContract.integrity: Each key has bounded ordered chunks, exact UTF-16 length and SHA-256. The marker stores immutable original-source and current full-envelope digests; revision 0 must equal the original source.
transactionalMigrationContract.originalCopy: Read and verify an existing immutable copy or preserve it durably before opening the target migration transaction. A different source cannot replace it.
transactionalMigrationContract.preparedLease: prepare() validates detached input, opens its own transaction, creates all target tables, writes six values, verifies them and inserts the version-1 completion marker without committing. Only the current prepared lease may commit or roll back.
transactionalMigrationContract.commit: Recheck prepared target integrity, require synchronous source verification while the caller still owns its writer pause, then commit all target data, schema and marker together. Verify committed state and preserved source afterward.
transactionalMigrationContract.rollback: An explicit rollback discards all prepared target objects and revokes its lease while preserving the separately committed original. Stale leases cannot commit or end a later preparation.
transactionalMigrationContract.restartAuthority: read() requires a complete valid marker, exact schema, all six value headers, bounded chunks and both current/original integrity. It returns committed SQLite state and revision; it never reads legacy storage or substitutes empty defaults.
transactionalMigrationContract.repeatMigration: A completed database is authoritative. A second preparation is refused before any mutation, including when legacy storage is older than a newer committed database revision.
transactionalMigrationContract.failurePolicy: Never automatically resume or close the legacy facade. Roll back only this operation's transaction, retain the primary sanitized error, poison uncertain repositories, and require a fresh connection after failures.
transactionalMigrationContract.ownershipLimit: The caller must own the entire connection for the lifetime of the repository and prepared lease, and coordinate every source context. Synchronous rechecks detect observed source changes; they are not a cross-store atomic lock.

mutableWriteContract.activation: Explicit on an already open, exclusively owned migrated connection; not used by production startup or existing synchronous legacy writers.
mutableWriteContract.batch: One to six unique allowlisted key/raw entries. Null means absence; strings retain exact UTF-16 including malformed inner JSON. Validate and detach caller inputs before the first await; reject excess size without truncation.
mutableWriteContract.revision: Require the caller expected revision to match the authoritative receipt inside the write transaction. A changed batch increments once using a bound compare-and-swap guarded by the previous revision and current/source digests, with mandatory read-back.
mutableWriteContract.noOp: An identical batch leaves the revision and every row unchanged. Transaction acknowledgements and integrity still require validation.
mutableWriteContract.atomicity: Update changed headers/chunks and the current digest/revision in one explicit transaction. Prepared writes remain uncommitted until their current lease commits; rollback and process interruption recover the entire prior revision.
mutableWriteContract.original: The immutable initial snapshot and source digest never change. Reads and commits validate the original as well as the current state; no automatic recreation or stale-source fallback.
mutableWriteContract.boundedNativeCalls: One SQL statement per execute/run, bound values and chunks of at most 16384 UTF-16 units. Never split valid surrogate pairs. Same 32 Mi UTF-16 total envelope bound.
mutableWriteContract.ownership: A prepared lease blocks other methods on the instance; stale leases cannot end later work. Refuse foreign transactions without committing or rolling them back. Caller ownership of the entire connection is required.
mutableWriteContract.failures: Rollback only owned work, preserve sanitized primary errors, and refuse repository reuse after storage uncertainty. A lost commit acknowledgement is an error requiring connection reopen and a read of the actual committed revision before retry.
mutableWriteContract.schemaVersion: Uses existing namespace schema version 1; does not change PRAGMA user_version, unrelated tables, legacy keys or backups.
mutableWriteContract.remainingIntegration: Pre-render bootstrap, source-context coordination, asynchronous UI persistence, backup imports/exports, recovery UX and real-device end-to-end checks.
